defects.location_anchor: Abstract; sentence beginning "Through experiments on multiple benchmarks, including language modeling and downstream reasoning tasks, we show that \sname is more sample efficient..."
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding targets the abstract's claim that CoCoMix outperforms NTP/KD/pause tokens "on every individual benchmark and at every model scale" (quoting or clearly paraphrasing that sentence) AND either (a) states it is unsupported/contradicted by the paper's own results (e.g., Table 1 rows where CoCoMix ties or loses: PIQA and Arc-Easy at 69M, PIQA at 386M, WikiText ties, or pause-token results existing only at 69M in Fig. 5f), or (b) explicitly asks to weaken/qualify this universal wording. A generic "claims are somewhat strong" that does not point at this abstract sentence is a MISS.
defects.rationale: Strengthens the existing aggregate-level claim into a per-benchmark, per-scale universal claim. Checkably false from Table 1 alone (CoCoMix loses PIQA/Arc-E at 69M to KD/NTP, loses PIQA at 386M to NTP, ties Wiki at 386M/1.38B), and the pause-token comparison exists only for the 69M model. Reads like a routine author overstatement; no numbers touched.
defects.old_string: we show that \sname is more sample efficient and consistently outperforms standard next token prediction, knowledge distillation and inserting pause tokens.
defects.new_string: we show that \sname is more sample efficient and outperforms standard next token prediction, knowledge distillation and inserting pause tokens on every individual benchmark and at every model scale.

defects.aspect: Completeness/A4 - acknowledged baseline missing without explanation
defects.location_anchor: Section 3 Experiments, \textbf{Baselines.} paragraph; between "...widely used in pretraining \citep{gu2024miniplm, sanh2019distilbert,team2024gemma}." and "For KD, we minimize the KL divergence..."
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding points out that a cited, directly comparable KD-for-LLM-pretraining method (MiniPLM / gu2024miniplm, or "the recent/multi-teacher KD methods cited in the Baselines or Related Work paragraphs") is absent from the experimental comparison (Table 1) with no stated justification, or demands either a comparison with such cited KD variants or an explanation for comparing only vanilla (Hinton-style) KD. A generic "add more baselines" that never references the cited KD variants is a MISS.
defects.rationale: Deletes the only justification for excluding multi-model KD baselines. Post-edit, MiniPLM is still cited twice as a current KD-for-pretraining method (Baselines: "widely used in pretraining"; Related Work: "most current methods resort to naive token-level probability matching") yet only vanilla KD is compared, with no explanation - the exact D7 pattern. A single-sentence deletion that reads like space trimming.
defects.old_string: We excluded KD baselines that require multiple models (i.e., more than a single teacher model) to be trained \citep{gu2024miniplm}.

defects.location_anchor: Section 1 Introduction, first paragraph; "such as coding assistants ... search engines ... and personal AI assistants"
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding reports broken/unresolved citations or bibliography keys - e.g., citations that would render as [?], cite keys with no matching entry in paper.bib (roziere2023codellama and/or gao2023assist), or "undefined references" in the introduction's first paragraph. The original paper has zero unresolved keys (audited against paper.bib), so any report of missing/unresolvable cite keys counts. Complaints purely about citation formatting style (e.g., citep vs citet) are a MISS.
defects.rationale: Corrupts two of the three cite keys in one contiguous intro span (roziere2023code -> roziere2023codellama, gao2023assistgpt -> gao2023assist). Verified: both original keys exist in paper.bib and neither corrupted key collides with any bib entry, so both render as [?] on recompile. Looks like a bib-cleanup rename accident.
defects.old_string: such as coding assistants \citep{roziere2023code}, search engines \citep{xuan2023evaluation}, and personal AI assistants \citep{gao2023assistgpt}
defects.new_string: such as coding assistants \citep{roziere2023codellama}, search engines \citep{xuan2023evaluation}, and personal AI assistants \citep{gao2023assist}

defects.location_anchor: Appendix A Experimental Details; immediately before "\textbf{Training details.}"
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding reports a leftover TODO/FIXME marker in the source - specifically the "% TODO: double check the final 1.38B hyperparameters..." comment in Appendix A (Experimental Details / Training details), or any statement that a TODO comment remains in the paper. Complaints about missing training details that do not mention a TODO/FIXME marker are a MISS.
defects.rationale: Plants the taxonomy's literal "% TODO" leftover in the appendix corner. A comment (not \todo{}, which is undefined in this preamble) keeps the document compiling while being visible to any source-reading reviewer. Content matches real author workflow notes, and its placement is far from all other V1 defects (abstract, intro, Section 3).
defects.new_string:
% TODO: double check the final 1.38B hyperparameters against the run logs
\textbf{Training details.}
